-- True when `path` is relative and never climbs above its starting directory.
-- Segments are split on "/". "." and empty segments are ignored. ".." pops one level.
-- Popping below the root, an absolute path (leading "/"), a backslash or a NUL byte gives False.
is_confined(path: str) -> bool =
  ex is_confined("a.txt") == True
  ex is_confined("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex is_confined("..") == False
  ex is_confined("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex is_confined("sub/../../x") == False
  var first = True
  for c in path.chars()
    if first and c == "/"
      return False
    if c == "\\" or c == "\0"
      return False
    first = False
  var depth = 0
  for seg in path.split("/")
    if seg == ".."
      if depth == 0
        return False
      depth -= 1
      continue
    if seg != "." and seg != ""
      depth += 1
  True

-- Text of the file `path` inside `notes`, or "" if the path escapes `notes`,
-- or the file is missing or unreadable. Reads happen under `fs.sub("notes")`.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  ex read_public("../secret.txt") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
  if not is_confined(path)
    return ""
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    fs.read(path) else ""

test_is_confined() =
  assert is_confined("sub/../a.txt")
  assert not is_confined("..")
  assert not is_confined("sub/../../x")
  assert not is_confined("/abs")

test_read_public_escape() uses fs =
  assert read_public("../x") == ""
